## Repeated differentiation {#gac2-key-ideas .gac-lesson}

<div class="gac2-key-ideas">
<p><strong>Differentiate again.</strong> The second derivative is the derivative of the first derivative.</p>
<p data-math="f''(x)=y''=\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}"></p>
<p><strong>Evaluate afterwards.</strong> Find the required derivative function, then substitute the given value.</p>
<p><strong>Check the domain.</strong> Any proposed value must belong to the domain of the required derivative.</p>
</div>

<p class="gac-prompt">Can <span data-math="f'(1)=0"></span> while <span data-math="f''(1)\ne0"></span>?</p>
<p class="gac-success"><strong>I can</strong> calculate second and higher derivatives, evaluate them at a given value and use the correct notation.</p>

::: notes
3 minutes. Yes: Example 1.6 gave f'(1)=0 and f''(1)=-6. A zero at one input does not mean the whole first derivative is the zero function. Ask students to explain why substituting first would have hidden this.

Revisit the success criterion and note that f^{(n)} denotes the n-th derivative. Students can add the definition, equivalent notation and evaluation order to the booklet's Key Ideas box. Keep the homework slide limited to the assigned work.
:::
